chapter: Friends, New York life and recording routine
title: Record pay, spending and clothes in the 1920s
summary: She was paid about a hundred dollars a record, supported her brother and husband's mother, and saved nothing.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: When did you make those? During the day?
Oh, yeah. I never was recording at night time. (Inaudible).
How much did they pay you for making a record in those years?
Well, they paid me -- I never did make but one record, I always made a gang of records. And then they would pay you dollars a record, you know. I mean, (unintelligible).

A hundred dollars a record, you know. If I made five or six records, I made a thousand dollars, you know, something like that. According to how many I make, you know, they give you some of it and some of it they mail to you. But they give me enough for my expenses (unintelligible).
Oh, they paid you that besides.
So you were doing very well in the '20s as a very young woman.
You were a very important person in the '20s.
Yeah. That's why I say they tell me that (unintelligible) I said, but I didn't know anything about it because I never (unintelligible).
Well, let me ask you this, Miss Wallace. Were you -- did you put some of that money in the bank?
No, I had my little brother, you know, (unintelligible) and I had my husband's mother (unintelligible).
So you took care of them all?

I took care of (unintelligible) was high and I had to buy furniture and furniture was high. My _______ bill was high. Everything was high. I didn't have no tuck -- no put-away money. (Unintelligible). I just
had money to live off of. (I didn't have no put-away money.
Now, the clothes you wore in the '20s. They were expensive, weren't they? The clothes, the dresses?

Yeah, but I didn't wear all that many dresses. I would get me a few dresses for street wear. Then I had different ______ stage wear, you know. My stage clothes, I (unintelligible) on the street (unintelligible) had me a suit or a dress or two or three (unintelligible) casual clothes, you know, (unintelligible). (Inaudible).
